subject.title: [Bug] jsonStore({ lock: true }) silently drops concurrent in-process updates: lock reentrancy is process-scoped, not owner-scoped

question: Should locked JSON stores preserve nested same-call-chain operations through owner-scoped reentrancy, or intentionally disallow them so every nested store operation waits and times out?
rationale: Both directions prevent the silent data loss, but they establish different compatibility contracts for existing callers that invoke a store again inside an update callback.

options.title: Use owner-scoped reentrancy
options.body: Preserve valid nested same-call-chain operations while forcing unrelated concurrent async callers to queue behind the lock.

options.title: Disable JSON-store reentrancy
options.body: Remove the JSON-store reentrancy opt-in and document that nested operations on the same locked store time out rather than bypassing serialization.

recommendation.title: Use owner-scoped reentrancy
recommendation.body: Preserve valid nested same-call-chain operations while forcing unrelated concurrent async callers to queue behind the lock.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent sidecar-lock refactor makes them the clearest available routing candidate for the lock-contract choice.
